page.layout: Running head at top centre with page number 244 at left. Two coin medallions side by side near the top, each with marginal legends (illustrations, legends transcribed below). Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs, with no notes or margins.

main_text.l: MAN·TVRC·IMP. [?] SVLEY[?]
ROSSA·VX [?] S·OL·
[The first word is printed in capitals.] SOLYMANUS Turcarum Rex, ex re feliciter prouisa,
cui euentus responderit, nomē tulisse fertur, quod Salomonem
Sapientiæ gloria inclytū, immutatis syllabis referat. Itaq; Soly-
mano secus ac patri contigisse constat, qui à contrario sensu
Selymus, hoc est mafuetus, autorque pacis, sit vocatus: quo ne-
mo Othomanorū ferocior & bellicosior fuerit. Sed Solymani
res gestæ, paternæ famæ nomen æquasse censeri possunt. Rece-
pta namque Syria, interfecto Gazelle qui rebellarat, Belgradū for-
titer expugnatū, Rhodus manu capta, Buda bis occupata, Au-
striacus exercitus in fuga cæsus, Rocādulphi ingentes copiæ ad
Budā superatæ, expugnatū Strigoniū, & Alba Regalis præclaræ
Hungariæ ciuitates, an. 1543. & paulò ante Hispani in Dalmatia
ad Castrum nouū expugnati, classibus eorum, quæ insuperabi-
les viderentur, ad Leucadem fugatis: hæc, inquā, Solymanum
patri, aufu nec imparem, nec gloriæ minus auidū testabuntur.
Assyriæ præterea & Mesopotamiæ regna, cum Babylonia vrbe,
magnæ Memphi æquada, quæ suo Solymanus adiecit Imperio,
captæ à patre Aegypto opponi possunt. Quinetiam Solymanus
maioris Armeniæ, Mediæ, Perfidisque fines, vsque ad sinū Per-
sicū, vastauit: Taurim Persarū Regiam, bis cepit: Tamasum So-
phim, Hismaëlis filium, refugientem ad mōtes, fugauit. Verum
quod ad Solymani mores etiā attinet, fatentur sanè Turcę, eius
subditi, eum suprà cæteros Othomannorum principes, qui per
ducentos regnarint annos, iustitiæ, sobrietatis, & continentiæ
laude clarissimum. Vide Paulum Iouium.
ROSSA omnium Solymani vxorum pulcherrima, præter
formā multis etiam virtutibus dotata est: quare apud Solyma-
num præ cæteris omnibus vxoribus maxima pollet gratia, ab
eóque vnicè amatur, ac colitur.

page.notes: The head running title reads "PROMPTV." with a doubtful glyph for P (possibly ligatured or Greek-like), transcribed as printed. The coin legends are read from the illustrations and are uncertain: the left legend and the right legend are partly unreadable, so [?] marks them. Spelling is as printed (e.g. "aufu", "Turcę", "Persicū"). The line break "Belgradū for / titer" has no printed hyphen and is written as "fortiter".
